ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Korean Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 6516, as amended through 2024, is the principal AML/CFT statute; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Proceeds of Crime Act), Act No. 6515, as amended; Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulations and examination standards; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25. Under the FTRA there is no public corporate UBO register; financial institutions must identify and verify beneficial owners holding 25 percent or more of member quotas and disclose such data to Korean government authorities and KoFIU only on lawful demand.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate shareholders, directors, managers, and authorized signatories must be screened before any filing against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States Treasury OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Sanctions Lists, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Korean government sanctions lists administered by the Financial Services Commission and the National Security Council. Politically Exposed Persons, both foreign and domestic, must be identified through risk-based questionnaires, adverse-media checks, and source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Screening must be repeated at every material event, at each mandatory annual review, and upon any sanctions-list update. Confirmed hits require immediate legal hold, asset freezing if applicable, escalation to the designated AML compliance officer, and submission of a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU under the FTRA. Enhanced due diligence must independently verify UBO identity using Korean corporate registry extracts, notarized identification documents, bank reference letters, and physical substance evidence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea i-ROS (Internet Registration Office) official company name search and registration portal for corporate registry filings
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, a corporate name must be expressed in the Korean alphabet using the statutory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign investors may use a Korean phonetic transliteration of their English brand, and an English parallel trade name may be recorded only after the Korean name has been accepted. The four-tier naming convention is: first, the distinguishing word or brand identifier; second, a business-purpose descriptive element; third, the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and fourth, the head-office administrative district. The registry compares exact Korean name strings for identity or confusing similarity, and an English name alone is never accepted as the registered corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term falsely implying a government, municipal, central-bank, or licensed financial institution affiliation requiring prior ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its counsel may file a written objection with the District Court Registration Office registry examiner within fourteen days under the Korean Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching the name-search result, the rejected filing receipt, the proposed transliteration, and any ministerial approval required for sensitive tokens. The registry examiner must re-examine the objection within twenty days and issue either an acceptance or a reasoned refusal. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply to the competent District Court for a judicial ruling, and the court ordinarily decides within thirty days. Immediately and in parallel, the applicant may submit a new name through i-ROS without forfeiting the appeal; however, the initial thirty-day pre-clearance validity window cannot be extended by appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a VPN network, digital encryption software, and privacy application business classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced under AML standards, Korean banks and the National Tax Service do not accept a virtual office or commercial mail-drop address as the registered place of business. The registered office must be the actual head office where management performs control functions under the Korean Commercial Act. A serviced office with a physical lease, dedicated desk space, signage, and on-site records is the minimum accepted substance. A pure virtual mailbox is rejected for business registration and for corporate bank account opening because the bank must conduct face-to-face CDD and the tax authority must be able to find the representative and records at the registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the National Tax Service or municipal tax authorities is 25 percent during the first 365 days after incorporation, rising during corporate tax filing and VAT registration cycles. Compliance checklist: visible company nameplate at the registered office; lease agreement in the company name; at least one full-time employee or director present during business hours; physical IT equipment or verifiable evidence of hosted infrastructure; incoming mail and correspondence received; statutory books and accounting records maintained; VAT and electronic tax invoice access available; board and member meeting minutes retained. Failure on items one through four will trigger a sham-office or deemed-dormant finding, administrative revocation of the business registration, and enhanced AML scrutiny of the corporate bank account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) provisions, Articles 287-2 through 287-74; Corporate Registration Regulations under the Court Organization Act; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act for banking; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-resident capital contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Division of the District Court (Dunggiso / deunggi-gwa) having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, operating under the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing available through the court registration e-service (e-court).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration of a Limited Liability Company (beobin deunggi sincheongseo) submitted together with the certified Articles of Incorporation, share subscription schedules, payment evidence, and corporate seal documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa. Capital may be set at any amount in the Articles of Incorporation. Contributions must be paid in full by each member before incorporation registration; no statutory blocked escrow account is required, but all capital must be deposited into a temporary corporate bank account and remain in the company's possession. Non-resident members must comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and, where applicable, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for inbound capital reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND INITIAL MEMBERS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The undersigned, being all initial members and the duly appointed managers of the entity described above in formation, solemnly resolve as follows. 1. Capital Subscription and Call. The total authorized membership capital, the value of each membership contribution unit, and the individual subscriptions stated in the Articles of Incorporation are hereby approved. The representative manager is directed to collect all subscribed capital in cleared Korean Won before the statutory incorporation registration is filed. For each contribution, the representative manager shall deposit funds into a temporary corporate bank account in the name of Yuhan Hoesa, issue a written contribution receipt, and prepare a complete member register and contribution schedule. No capital may be returned to any member, and no distribution of contributions may occur, until incorporation registration is completed and all statutory liabilities are satisfied. 2. Banking Authorization. The company shall maintain real-name, transparent financial accounts in the Republic of Korea. The representative manager and the manager designated in the Articles of Incorporation are jointly authorized to open corporate current and savings accounts with any reputable Korean commercial bank, complete know-your-customer and anti-money laundering procedures, execute bank signature cards, establish online banking credentials, designate transaction limits, and serve as authorized signatories for all corporate deposit, withdrawal, transfer, and foreign exchange transactions. The bank is instructed to honor all payment orders and cheques executed in accordance with the signature card, subject to the oversight of the Board. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office address stated in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the company's statutory seat. The representative manager is directed to obtain the lease agreement, landlord consent certificate, and premises-use authorization, and to file such address with the District Court Registration Office, the National Tax Service, and the relevant local tax office. All statutory notices and corporate records shall be maintained at such office. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following officers are appointed: the representative manager, who shall have authority to act as the statutory legal representative and principal executive officer; and a regular manager, who shall jointly supervise ordinary business operations and, if required by the Commercial Act, shall serve as statutory auditor. Each officer accepts the fiduciary duties of care and loyalty, shall maintain books and records required by the External Audit Act, and shall cause the company to comply with the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, the Personal Information Protection Act, and all applicable data security laws. 5. Delegation of Formation Formalities. All officers are directed to execute all applications, powers of attorney, appointment certificates, tax filings, registration tax payments, and supplementary documents necessary to complete corporate registration, business registration, and banking activation. Any prior actions taken in connection with formation are ratified. These resolutions were adopted unanimously and are effective as of the date of execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Signature Authentication of the Articles of Incorporation and Formation Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public under the Korean Notaries Association or the District Court Registration Office for signature authentication where required by counsel or a bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial members shall prepare and execute Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in full compliance with Commercial Act Articles 287-2 through 287-74. The Articles must state the corporate name, the registered office address, the business purpose limited to ISIC 6201 covering virtual private network software, digital encryption, network security SaaS, and related software services, the amount of each contribution, the contribution unit price, the number of units, the method of contribution payment, the names of managers, and the representative manager. Each member shall sign and seal the Articles personally or through a lawfully appointed attorney-in-fact. If the court or bank requests notarization, the formation attorney shall arrange for all signatures to be certified before a notary public with identification documents. After execution, a certified copy of the Articles, a copy of the incorporation minutes, and a specimen of the corporate seal shall be prepared for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or government-issued identification of each member and officer
Foreign entity registration certificate or certificate of good standing with apostille and certified Korean translation if a member is a corporation
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean with signed corporate seal specimen
Minutes of the incorporation meeting and first board resolution
Power of attorney for the local formation agent
Consent to use registered office from the landlord or a certified copy of the lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the authenticity of signatures or foreign documents, cure by obtaining an apostille, a licensed Korean translation, an updated corporate certificate, and a supplemental signature authentication. If the business purpose is considered too broad or not compliant, amend the objects clause to be strictly limited to software development, VPN technology, encryption, and digital network security services, then re-execute the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Corporate Registration at the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Division of the District Court (Dunggiso) with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, via in-person submission or the e-court electronic registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation attorney shall submit the application for corporate registration together with the certified Articles of Incorporation, the initial members' minutes, the contribution payment confirmation, the leaseholder consent, identification of the representative manager, and the registered office documentation. The registry examiner will verify legal form, name availability, whether the corporate purpose is lawful, whether the capital contribution is fully paid, and whether all statutory officers are validly appointed. Upon approval, the registry will issue an official corporate registration certificate evidencing the legal existence of Yuhan Hoesa. The attorney shall immediately order a certified corporate seal certificate for the representative manager and keep a certified copy of the registration certificate for subsequent business and bank filings.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate registration
Certified copy of the finalized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the incorporation meeting and first board resolution
Proof of capital contribution payment such as bank receipt and contribution schedule
Lease agreement and landlord consent certificate
Identification of the representative manager and regular manager
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Registration tax and education surcharge payment receipt
Corporate seal certificate application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration office issues a request for correction or a period for supplementation, submit the corrective document through the same registry window within the stated period. Where the name conflicts with an existing corporate name, choose a secondary reserved name from the name search and file an amendment to the Articles. If the registered office consent is questioned, provide a certified copy of the lease and a building owner usage confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Taxpayer Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, Hometax online system, or the local district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty-one days after the corporate registration certificate is issued, the representative manager or the formation attorney shall apply for a business registration certificate under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The application must identify the corporation as a software and digital network security service provider, with VAT registration for the supply of VPN and encryption SaaS services. The tax office will assign a corporate business registration number, which functions as the corporate taxpayer identification number. The company must also register the place of business to comply with corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding obligations. Since the company is a pure digital service provider and not a physical manufacturer, the business registration certificate is the sole operating tax authorization required.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate issued by the District Court
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement for the registered office and landlord consent
Representative manager's valid identification
Corporate seal certificate
Bank account opening certificate or temporary deposit statement
Completed business registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service requests additional foreign investment declarations or tax compliance history, submit the Foreign Investment Promotion Act declaration and certified corporate documents. If the tax office categorizes the activity as a telecommunications license service, submit a written protest explaining that the activity is software and SaaS under ISIC 6201 and is not a statutory telecommunications operator requiring a separate license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Corporate Bank Account and Verifying Paid-in Capital at a Licensed Korean Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea acting under the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative manager shall appear in person at the chosen Korean bank branch with the corporate registration certificate, certified Articles, corporate seal certificate, and valid identification. The bank will perform know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering checks on the company, its officers, and its ultimate beneficial owners. Because Yuhan Hoesa is a digital software company with no industrial plant, the bank will rely on the registered office lease and corporate registration to evidence physical presence. The temporary subscription account, if used before registration, shall be closed and the paid-in capital transferred into the main operating account in the corporate name. The bank shall issue a paid-in capital certificate if required, and the representative manager shall set up online banking authority in accordance with the board resolution.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate of the representative manager
Valid passport or alien registration card of the representative manager
Temporary capital deposit account statement or contribution payment receipt
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration and AML questionnaire
Registered office lease agreement and utility bill or building certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening application due to enhanced AML review, submit a corporate organization chart, source of funds statement, and bank reference letters. If the bank disputes the physical address, provide a certified copy of the lease and a signed landlord confirmation of the company's right to operate from the registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. Yuhan Hoesa is a pure digital/software company classified under ISIC 6201, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. No industrial manufacturing license is required from the Korean Industrial Complex authority or municipal industrial licensing bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No operating license, manufacturing permit, or assembly authorization is required. The company only needs the standard business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service and any ministerial license under the Information and Communications Technology framework only if the VPN service is ever reclassified as an electronic communications operator; the current scope expressly excludes such activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea / Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. The project does not involve physical infrastructure, industrial facilities, chemical processes, manufacturing, or warehousing; therefore no full Environmental Impact Assessment, prior environmental review, or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no wastewater discharges, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous chemical storage, or industrial waste streams. The company's office operations must comply with the general Waste Control Act and Water Supply and Waterworks Act for ordinary domestic sewage and office waste, and must dispose of IT hardware and spent electronic equipment under the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense fire permits or industrial fire safety licensing. For the leased office premises, the building owner shall provide the official fire safety completion certificate issued by the municipal fire department for the building. The company shall otherwise comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for workplace safety, for example providing a safe office environment and ergonomic workspaces, and with the Act on Fire Prevention and Firefighting for portable fire extinguishers and emergency exits in the office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); export declarations and customs clearance are processed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa incorporated under the Commercial Act, the domestic representative must file a Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office (Head of District Tax Office) via HomeTax or in person within 20 days after business commencement. The applicant must submit the corporate registration certificate from the Korean court registry, articles of incorporation, board resolution appointing the domestic representative, lease agreement or occupancy certificate for the registered business address, and a passport or identification card of the representative. Because the entity is a foreign-invested company, the shareholders should also obtain a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and submit the certificate of foreign exchange bank dealing. The NTS issues a single 10-digit Business Registration Number which simultaneously serves as the corporate TIN and VAT registration number. A non-resident foreign corporation without a Korean place of business does not use the ordinary Yuhan Hoesa registration path; it instead registers through a domestic tax representative as a foreign business operator under the Value-Added Tax Act, providing the foreign entity name, overseas address, description of business, global head office details, and the tax representative's Korean information. In the VPN SaaS context, the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is the principal VAT registrant and will carry its own Korean Business Registration Number for all domestic supplies and zero-rated export supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea has no check-the-box entity classification election and no comparable US-style hybrid mismatch election for a Yuhan Hoesa. The entity is conclusively treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and no pass-through default is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa there is no economic turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory upon business commencement regardless of revenue. For non-resident foreign suppliers of services consumed in Korea, registration becomes mandatory when Korean taxable supplies exceed the statutory de minimis threshold, in which case a simplified foreign business operator VAT registration is obtained through the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory and must be transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system by the day following the supply date for all supplies between VAT-registered Korean businesses. HomeTax assigns a digital signature to each issued e-tax invoice, and the issuer must retain and transmit the approved e-tax invoice XML; there is no separate real-time customs clearance or physical anti-fraud stamp requirement for the VPN SaaS supply. Retail supplies to Korean end consumers are also subject to cash receipt issuance through NTS-approved cash receipt devices, with statutory penalties for failure to issue e-invoices or cash receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 11 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods and qualifying services are zero-rated. VPN network privacy and digital encryption software supplies qualify as zero-rated services when the buyer is a non-resident, the place of supply is stipulated as outside Korea in the contract, the service is used entirely outside Korea, and payment is received in foreign currency from abroad. Goods exports require a formal Customs Act export declaration filed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. The Korean exporter must substantiate the actual export by maintaining an export contract, commercial invoice, customs export declaration, transport documents, and foreign exchange receipt evidence. For zero-rated SaaS, the Yuhan Hoesa must also issue a zero-rated electronic tax invoice through HomeTax and retain evidence of the foreign customer's non-resident status and overseas consumption or use of the VPN service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Certificate filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice issued by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation / Certificate of Purchase of Export Proceeds issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank
Export or service contract identifying the foreign buyer, scope of VPN/digital services, place of supply, and settlement currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited by the NTS using data matching between HomeTax e-tax invoices, Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS exports, and Korean foreign exchange bank records. If the supply is not proven to be genuinely exported, if the VPN SaaS service is deemed used or received in Korea, or if the export proceeds are not repatriated into Korea within the required deadline, the zero-rated treatment is reversed and 10% VAT is assessed with statutory additional taxes, interest, and possible criminal penalties. Issuance of false zero-rated e-tax invoices also exposes the entity to separate penalty taxes up to 2% of the relevant supply value under the Value-Added Tax Act, and abusive claims may trigger a clawback of input VAT previously recovered and addition of overdue tax surcharges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) operated by the Korea Exchange Bank (KEB Hana) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with full convertibility for trade in goods, services, and routine profit remittances. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections, intercompany loans, and portfolio investments, are generally free but subject to a declaration or reporting requirement through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The Korean won (KRW) is not a freely deliverable offshore currency; non-resident accounts and offshore won trading are heavily restricted. Surrender requirements apply to export proceeds: all foreign currency earned from exports must be either repatriated or deposited into a domestic foreign currency account within 18 months from the date of acquisition, with no mandatory conversion into KRW for proceeds held in foreign currency accounts. However, converting to KRW is required if the entity seeks to fund local payroll and KRW-denominated operating expenses. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted without prior approval, but a foreign exchange bank must verify the source of funds and the underlying tax clearance (e.g., withholding tax certificate under the Korea Tax Treaty). A material hurdle is that any capital contribution exceeding USD 1 million equivalent must be reported to the delegated foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the remittance, and for FDI, a prior notification to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy is required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Overall, the regime is compliant and functional for legitimate SaaS/network security businesses, but any use of virtual assets, crypto settlement, or privacy wallets will trigger enhanced scrutiny and likely rejection of the banking application.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 14 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be collected and repatriated to a domestic foreign currency account or brought into Korea within 18 months from the date of export (with extension possible only for exceptional causes such as arbitration or litigation). There is no mandatory conversion rate for export proceeds; however, if the company needs KRW liquidity, it must sell the foreign currency to any licensed foreign exchange bank at the prevailing market rate. For digital services (SaaS, VPN subscriptions, app sales) treated as exports of intellectual property/software, the 18-month collection period applies, and the service provider must register the transaction with the designated foreign exchange bank using the appropriate revenue code (e.g., case number under 'Earnings from Software' – code 521100). Failure to repatriate within the statutory window triggers administrative fines, retroactive tax assessments, and customs investigation referrals.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Kookmin Bank (KB Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) + Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR)
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Operational Foreign Currency Account
Foreign Currency Current Account + KRW Settlement Account with integrated FEIS reporting
Basic Operational Currency Account + Foreign Currency Time Deposit for surplus liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low / Non-Viable. South Korean regulations under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Act on Registration of Financial Businesses require any entity providing foreign exchange services or payment settlement to be licensed as a 'Foreign Exchange Business Operator' or registered as an 'Electronic Financial Business Operator' with the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Cross-border digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) do not hold a Korean foreign exchange license and are legally barred from maintaining on-shore KRW settlement accounts or providing local IBANs/routing numbers. They can only serve Korean entities as a receiving conduit for offshore USD/EUR, but cannot facilitate KRW payouts to Korean vendors or employees. Therefore, the company must maintain a primary relationship with a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank. For global collections, the company may use Stripe or Paymentwall as payment gateways that route settlement funds to the company's designated domestic bank account via SWIFT. However, these gateways do not replace the domestic banking relationship; they merely act as payment aggregators collecting customer funds offshore and remitting net proceeds as a single wire. The bank will require a business contract and gateway settlement statements to verify the source of funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in-branch is mandatory for all statutory directors (including foreign non-resident directors) at the time of corporate account opening under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 10 and the Korean 'Real Name Financial Transactions Act'. The bank's compliance officer must verify the identity of the beneficial owner, the director's real-name identification (foreign registration card or passport), and a documented source of funds. Remote consular proxy opening is strictly not permitted for newly formed KR entities without at least one in-person visit. Exception: If the foreign director cannot travel, the company can appoint a local compliance attorney under a notarized power-of-attorney to appear with the director's certified true passport, apostilled corporate documents, and a video call interview administered by the bank's international branch. However, most Tier-1 banks still demand the final sign-off from the resident director who is registered as the company's statutory representative. For a Yuhan Hoesa with all foreign directors, the prudent path is to appoint a Korean resident director or open the account in the name of the local branch (if registered) following a physical due diligence visit by a bank representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-Risk Jurisdiction Nexus: The VPN/privacy app business model may obscure the identity of end customers, and the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction may be a tax haven or a high-risk third country (e.g., British Virgin Islands, Panama, or UAE). The bank will flag this as potential money laundering through digital services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a full org chart showing the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with passport copy and proof of clean source of wealth (e.g., audited financial statements of the parent, salary slips, and tax returns for the last 3 years); (2) a notarized and apostilled Certificate of Existence and Good Standing from the UBO's home jurisdiction; (3) a business plan detailing the SaaS subscription model, target customer countries, and a ban on sales to any persons in jurisdictions under OFAC, EU, or Korean sanctions; (4) a signed Declaration of No Derivative Instruments or crypto-denominated payments from customers; and (5) a list of the underlying payment processors (Stripe, Paymentwall) with their own AML/KYC certifications and PCI-DSS evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Software/SaaS Export Mismatch: VPN services are treated as 'telecommunications/network’ services under Korean tax law, but the company may register as ISIC 6201 (computer programming). The bank will flag a discrepancy between the declared business scope and the actual revenue stream, leading to a possible 'false statement' or 'abnormal transaction' alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certification from a licensed Korean tax attorney (tax accountant) confirming that VPN and network privacy app development qualifies as 'Computer Programming, Consultancy and Related Activities' under the Korean Standard Industrial Classification (KSIC) code 6201, and that the revenue is classified as 'Software Service Export' under Article 24 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Include an official Korean Language business description from the company registry, and a sample software licensing agreement demonstrating that the customer pays for the right to use the encryption software, not for access to a telecommunications facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk Collection of Low-Value Digital Payments: The company will receive thousands of small-dollar payments via Stripe and Paymentwall from anonymous internet users. Banks impose 'transaction monitoring threshold filtering' and will flag a structured pattern of similar incoming wire amounts (e.g., USD 9.99 per month) as potential layering or unauthorized money transmission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (a) a signed annual settlement agreement from Stripe and Paymentwall detailing the merchant category code (MCC 5815 – Digital Goods – Media, Books, Movies, Music), the holdback reserves, and the payout schedule; (b) a transaction monitoring dashboard snapshot showing that the payments are collected from registered user accounts with device intelligence, email verification, and IP address geolocation; (c) a technical whitepaper of the VPN service demonstrating that the service cannot function without user identity and that all refunds are processed through the original payment method; and (d) an independent audit report from a reputable accounting firm confirming that no cash-like virtual assets are used and that each settlement trace matches the invoiced subscriber IDs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign Director Non-Residency and Tax Residency Ambiguity: The bank's KYC system may classify the company as a 'shell company' because all statutory directors are foreign non-residents and there is no Korean office, payroll, or physical asset, creating a high-risk classification under Article 39-3 of the Specific Financial Information Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) a notarized Office Lease Agreement for a registered Korean business address (even a virtual office or shared workspace with a physical address); (2) a certificate of local tax compliance (scheduled corporate tax payment or null tax return filed with the Korea National Tax Service); (3) an appointment letter for a local AML compliance officer (i.e., an external accounting firm or law firm) who will be responsible for internal controls and transaction validation; and (4) a declaration that all board meetings are conducted with dual signatory approval (two directors) on all bank payments above KRW 100 million, with board minutes countersigned by a Korean notary public.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections (shareholder loans or equity contributions) must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank and reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The proper protocol is: (1) receive a prior notification certificate ('K-Benchmark' / foreign investment report) from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or a delegated Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) center; (2) open a KRW-denominated foreign investment account or a non-resident won account at the chosen Tier-1 bank; (3) remit the capital injection via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's corporate bank, with the purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment into Software Company' (e.g., code 831100 – Investment in a local company) and the clear name of the foreign investor; (4) upon receipt, the bank will verify the source of funds, converting the foreign currency into KRW at the prevailing market rate and delivering a 'Certificate of Foreign Currency Deposit & Purchase'; (5) the company must issue new shares within 30 days of the remittance and file a post-report with MOTIE. For shareholder loans exceeding USD 3 million equivalent, the bank will require a certified loan agreement and will enforce an arm's-length interest rate to avoid thin capitalization or disguised equity. Any inbound transfer from a personal bank account, a separated shell, or a jurisdiction not in the investor's UBO tax profile will be blocked and reported under suspicious transaction reporting (STR).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the VPN/privacy app business primarily involve (a) paying foreign cloud hosting providers (AWS, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean), (b) paying international subcontractors or licensing fees, and (c) distributing dividends to foreign shareholders. For cloud infrastructure payments, the company must execute a SWIFT MT103 with a corporate-to-corporate instruction, using purpose code 'IT and Cloud Computing Service Purchase' (e.g., under the Export-Import of Services classification, code 724000 – Computer and IT Services). For dividend distributions, the outbound remittance requires (1) an audited balance sheet showing distributable retained earnings, (2) a board resolution for dividend declaration, (3) a tax withholding certificate proving 22% corporate withholding tax (or reduced treaty rate if the shareholder is a treaty-eligible jurisdiction), and (4) the local foreign exchange bank's confirmation that no outstanding borrowings exceed the statutory limits. Trade finance structures such as commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C) are not applicable for digital services; however, for future reselling of hardware tokenized security keys (hardware VPN dongles), the company may use a documentary collection or an irrevocable L/C only if the bank confirms the underlying commercial invoice and bill of lading. Given the digital nature, the dominant clearing rail is direct SWIFT MT103 in USD/EUR. The Korean Bank Federation's 'BOK-Wire+' system is used for domestic KRW transfers, but cross-border disbursements cannot be netted without a full compliance review for each wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (plain vanilla watertight forwards) up to 12 months, for hedging expected export proceeds denominated in USD/EUR, provided the underlying invoice and subscriber revenue forecast is documented and the amount does not exceed the projected net insurance value of future export earnings.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW are permissible only between resident banking institutions and non-resident counterparties under the Korea Foreign Exchange Brokerage Act; the domestic entity cannot directly execute an NDF with an offshore bank without going through a licensed local bank's international desk. The notional principal must be tied to a verifiable commercial transaction.

Currency swaps (foreign exchange swaps) are limited to converting USD/EUR proceeds into KRW for operational liquidity, with a maximum tenor of one year, requiring a board resolution and a monthly mark-to-market report to the bank's treasury department.

Options are restricted to zero-premium collar structures approved by the bank's derivatives committee; naked options or speculative positions are not permitted for a non-financial corporation under the Defense of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act's 'Real Demand Principle'.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Continued Maintenance and Changes in Registered Particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual renewal exists; new registration must be filed within 20 days from business commencement and any change in registered office, legal representative, or business description must be reported within 14 days after the change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report changes within 14 days triggers a general negligence surcharge under the Framework Act on National Taxes, administrative de-registration of the business place as a dormant business, and asset seizure for assessed tax; prolonged inactivity may lead to court-ordered dissolution of the company for failure to maintain a genuine registered office

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer the due date is 31 March, with an automatic one-month extension to 30 April if audited financial statements are required and an extension application is filed before the original due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax, under-reporting penalty of 10%, fraudulent under-reporting penalty of 30%, plus statutory delinquency interest at approximately 0.022% per day or the current NTS daily rate on unpaid taxes; continued arrearage allows attachment of bank accounts, seizure of receivables and tangible assets, and, if the company becomes wholly inactive, dissolution after a court strike-off action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax on Corporate Income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax authority (Si/Gun/Gu) via the Korea Local-Tax online portal (WeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the corporate income tax return due date; for a calendar-year normal filer the deadline is 30 April, and if the corporate income tax return is extended to 30 April, the local income tax return is due by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing attracts a negligence surcharge of up to 20% of the unpaid local income tax plus monthly delinquency surcharges on unpaid local tax; prolonged non-payment permits garnishment of bank deposits and compulsory sale of corporate property, but does not itself create an annual strike-off event

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Returns (Preliminary and Final Half-Year Returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer: preliminary first-quarter return due by 25 April; final first-half return due by 25 July; preliminary third-quarter return due by 25 October; final second-half return due by 25 January of the following year; if the date falls on a holiday, the next business day applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligence surcharge of 10% of the omitted VAT for unregistered or unfiled tax and 20% for a completely unfiled return, plus statutory daily delinquency interest; continued failure to file may result in estimated assessment by the NTS, enforcement seizure of assets, and cancellation of the business registration for chronic non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regular Members Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct regulatory filing; minutes and signed financial statements must be kept at the registered office and made available to the NTS and external auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year, or such shorter period fixed in the articles of incorporation, the annual regular meeting of members must be convened and the financial statements formally approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting or to approve financial statements invalidates reliance on limited-liability governance defenses, exposes the representative member to fiduciary liability, and permits the tax authorities to disregard the approved statements in audit proceedings; there is no annual registry strike-off for AGM failure, but the court may dissolve the company if it is unable to pass resolutions due to a deadlocked governance structure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing on DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), Republic of Korea, via the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the external auditor signs the audit report and before the annual members meeting for ratification; an audited-company postponement of the AGM also postpones the DART filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the statutory audit report on DART exposes the company and representative officer to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million and the NTS may deny tax-return deductions dependent on audited financial statements; a misleading or omitted audit report may be used as grounds for revocation of business licenses for regulated subsidiaries but is not an automatic company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Change Report and Shareholding Transfer Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA); change of registered particulars filed at the local District Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any foreign investor acquisition, disposal, or change in equity percentage must be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days after the transaction; amendments to the company registration file at the local District Court Registry are due within 30 days for any change in capital, members, or representation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the foreign-ownership change report may render the foreign investment ineligible for protection under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and subject to administrative fines up to KRW 20 million; failure to register changed governance particulars with the court can lead to a court-imposed administrative penalty and loss of power to file lawsuits through the representative in certain cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit and Accounting of Companies, an independent audit by a licensed Korean certified public accountant (CPA) is legally mandatory if the company's total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million); a listed or publicly-offered stock company is mandatory regardless of asset size; a company below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold may nevertheless be required to appoint an external auditor if it is designated as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission, if it is a financial institution, if it receives government funds under special legislation, or if shareholders representing at least 10% of shares demand a special audit under the same Act. Turnover and headcount thresholds are not statutory triggers for mandatory external audit in Korea, but an entity with fewer than 100 employees and total assets below KRW 12 billion is generally treated as a small company and is exempt from the external-audit mandate unless a special designation is made.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Republic of Korea are required for companies subject to the external-audit regime that meet the K-IFRS application criteria; non-public companies may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), and qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises if they are below the statutory external-audit asset threshold and are not public-interest entities. Accounting records and vouchers must be retained for the mandated statutory period, with the Commercial Act requiring 7 years for accounting books and 10 years for commercial and business records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a standalone public UBO annual return for an ordinary Yuhan Hoesa, but the Commercial Act obligates the company to maintain and update the member ledger upon every share transfer; a transfer of membership in a limited liability company is perfected only after the transferee is recorded in the register of members. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investor must file a change report with KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of any acquisition or disposal of equity. Under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, the company must keep beneficial-owner and customer identity records for 7 years and, if requested by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), must file beneficial-ownership information; an annual positive confirmation of the UBO schedule is required at the regular members meeting, and any material change in shareholding or control during the year must be captured by amending the member ledger, the board/minutes book, and the tax-registration records within the same 30-day change window. If the entity later becomes a virtual-asset service provider, payment institution, or other AML-regulated business, KoFIU annual beneficial-ownership confirmation will become directly mandatory.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Financial Statements and Audit Reports for at least 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per annum for a corporate secretarial agent or registered-office service provider in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a small Yuhan Hoesa below the statutory audit threshold; approximately USD 8,000 - 35,000 per annum for a mandatory CPA audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP, depending on total assets, transactional volume, and the VPN/SaaS revenue complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (maximum statutory Corporate Tax Act rate; progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% up to KRW 20 billion; 21% up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Free Economic Zone / R&D-intensive businesses may obtain 100% corporate tax holiday for 5 years and 50% for 2 years; additional R&D super-deduction under Tax Incentive Control Law; foreign direct investment tax credits; patent box regime not separately codified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Taxbase Computation Schedule under Article 60 of the Korean Corporate Tax Act, filed through National Tax Service HomeTax (Hometax) at hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis; semi-annual preliminary corporate tax returns due by the two-month deadline for the first six months)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is March 31; delinquent deadlines trigger surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, legal form, place of effective management, industry code (ISIC 6201), and resident vs non-resident classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter business registration number (BRN), Korean principal office, and foreign controlling shareholder information; if foreign-owned, attach a beneficial ownership schedule showing ultimate parent and voting percentage. The entity is a Korean resident corporation by incorporation, but foreign shareholder details feed withholding and CbCR obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax as presented in Korean GAAP/IFRS financial statements, with additions and deductions to reconcile book income to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For VPN subscription revenue, defer unearned revenue and recognize pro-rata over service terms; capitalise or expense software development costs according to Korean tax rules; exhibit physical server hosting expense and cloud infrastructure invoices; foreign parent service expenses must be supported by contracts and evidence of actual performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for non-deductible expenditures, excessive entertainment, book reserve disallowances, and transactions disallowed under tax avoidance provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ignore deductions for management fees, royalties, or interest paid to foreign affiliates unless arm's length; report related-party settlements in the international transaction schedule; NTS may reclassify excessive interest as constructive dividend subject to 22% withholding in a thin-capitalisation or hidden capital contribution audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before credits and after deducting loss carryforwards, with the taxpayer declaring tax loss carryforward utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean-source losses may reduce Korean taxable income; do not offset a foreign head office loss. If the Korean LLC has a foreign permanent establishment, allocate Korean net profit after applying Article 7 of the relevant DTA and observe the 5-year loss carryforward cap under the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax computed using the progressive rate schedule, plus the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on the assessed national corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive rates: 9% on income up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; compute the 10% local surtax; include a foreign tax credit reconciliation for foreign-source income supported by a Tax Residency Certificate and exemption method if treaty provides.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax credits, R&D and employment incentive deductions, and special free-zone or investment tax incentives claimed by the taxpayer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not directly claim these credits. The Korean entity should attach R&D expense details (software development, encryption research) and FEZ eligibility certificates; excessive foreign investor deductions without substance will be scrutinised; also disclose any withholding credit for tax withheld at source by Korean payers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of international related-party transactions and transfer pricing method used for goods, services, intangibles, loans, and rent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cloud hosting payments, VPN licensing fees, marketing support services, and intercompany loans to foreign affiliates. If total cross-border related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold, attach the Local/Master File; otherwise use the simplified report. Clearly identify CUP/resale/cost-plus/TNMM/profit-split and document comparable searches.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation and foreign remittance summary: dividends, interest, royalties, and technical service fees paid to non-resident shareholders, lenders, licensors or service providers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the gross amount paid, domestic withholding amount (22% composite rate if no treaty), treaty-reduced rate applied, and Tax Residency Certificate reference number. Beneficial ownership declarations must be obtained before payment; late withholding attracts liability for the unwithheld tax, daily penalties and possible criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a 20% negligence penalty for late or non-filing of the corporate tax return and a 10% negligence penalty for underreporting (increased to 30% for tax evaded above the statutory KRW 300 million threshold); daily delinquency charges of 0.03% accrue until payment; criminal prosecution under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can impose imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50 million; failure to file local-file documentation also triggers independent document penalties under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory composite rate on gross dividends paid to non-resident corporations (20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax), unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty and the beneficial ownership condition is satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must hold a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residence state, complete a beneficial ownership declaration and the domestic form for treaty-based reduced withholding, and provide the Korean withholding agent with the original or certified copy and certified translation before payment. The payer files the treaty withholding rate application with the National Tax Service through HomeTax; the foreign recipient must be legally entitled to the treaty benefits and satisfy limitation-on-benefits / principal purpose test. Retroactive refund of excess withholding is available by filing a tax refund claim within five years, but administrative penalties may apply if abuse is detected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-resident licensors for VPN software, patents, digital content or know-how are subject to 22% statutory WHT (20% national + 2% local); interest on intercompany debt is subject to 22% statutory WHT; applicable DTA generally reduces royalties and interest to 10%-15% depending on the treaty and beneficial owner status. Thin-capitalisation or arm's length denial can cause excessive interest to be re-characterised as non-deductible dividend, raising effective withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion cross-border related-party transactions with KRW 100 billion revenue threshold for Master File preparation; KRW 10 billion cross-border related-party transaction threshold for Local File preparation; smaller related-party transactions must still be disclosed on the annual corporate tax return schedule and retained in contemporaneous documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although South Korea does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, the National Tax Service will test economic substance under the substance-over-form doctrine, Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act, the international anti-avoidance rules in LEIITA, and treaty limitation-on-benefits/principal-purpose tests. For a VPN network SaaS company, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) such as contract execution, network management, encryption development, server control and customer acceptance must be conducted by employees in Korea, not merely routed through a paper Korean entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting non-resident VPN subscription revenue or using hidden Stripe/Paymentwall merchant accounts to receive Korean-source digital service fees without recording them in the corporate books and CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% negligence penalty for late/non-filing, 10% understatement penalty (30% if understatement exceeds KRW 300 million), plus daily delinquency charge of 0.03%; Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act, directors who intentionally or negligently cause the entity to evade tax are jointly liable to the tax authority for the amount of tax plus penalties; the director's name may be placed on the National Tax Service's overdue/blacklist registry, departure from Korea may be restricted, and fraudulent concealment of assets to evade collection is separately indictable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Base Erosion and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to document intercompany transactions or artificially inflating royalties and cloud-hosting fees paid to a foreign related VPN technology provider, leaving no taxable profit in the Korean entity while deducting large outbound payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under LEIITA, the NTS may adjust taxable income and increase the tax paid plus a 20% transfer pricing negligence penalty where bookkeeping documentation is incomplete; excessive interest or royalty payments are denied and 22% withholding tax is additionally collected on the disguised dividend or constructive remittance; non-filing of transfer pricing schedules triggers separate document penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Commercial Act Article 401 permits recovery of additional tax, penalties and interest from directors; foreign directors with expatriate status may be subject to travel bans under the National Tax Collection Act; repeated intentional evasion through abusive transfer pricing can result in criminal indictment and imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the VPN company as a Korean shell that lacks employees, office premises, server infrastructure, and board decision-making substance, and using the Korean entity solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid CFC reporting for the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may apply Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act and LEIITA general anti-abuse rules to disregard the entity or recharacterise transactions; denial of DTA relief under the principal purpose test, repayment of taxes, and additional underreporting penalties up to 20% (or 30% when the understated tax exceeds KRW 300 million); criminal sanctions under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if the substance failure is part of a fraudulent scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable to third-party creditors and the tax authority if the shell's separate personality is criminally abused; Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the entity is fictitious and compliance obligations are ignored; directors face asset freezing orders, a travel ban, and imprisonment for fraudulent concealment of foreign accounts or unreported VPN fee income.
